memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Consecrate those parts of the ordination ram that belong to Aaron and his sons: the breast that was waved and the thigh that was presented. This is always to be the perpetual share from the Israelites for Aaron and his sons. It is the contribution the Israelites are to make to the Lord from their fellowship offerings." - Exodus 29:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God assigns a portion of the offering to Aaron and his sons as their perpetual share. The priests had no farmland and no inheritance of territory; they served the tabernacle full-time. So God provided for them through the offerings of the people. Those who served at the altar were fed from the altar.

This is God's care in practical form. He does not call people into service and then leave them to fend for themselves. He arranged their provision as deliberately as He arranged their duties. And He built it into the community — the people's offerings sustained those who ministered among them.

Paul draws on this exact arrangement when teaching about supporting those in ministry, noting that those who serve at the altar share in what is offered there, and that in the same way the Lord has commanded that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from it (1 Cor 9:13-14). Two applications follow. If you serve God, trust Him to provide. And if others serve you spiritually, take seriously your part in supporting them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I trust God to provide as I serve Him?
Am I doing my part to support those who minister to me spiritually?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You provide for those who serve You and call Your people to share in that provision. Help me trust Your provision, and be generous toward those who serve me spiritually. Amen.
